text:
alex: starting the publish window for py + ts clients (cohort A). canary at 5% orgs, holdback 95%. i will trigger deploy-bot in ~10m. please pause any unrelated publishes in this window.

alex: rollout plan: 1) npm publish canary tag -> 2) pip wheels to staging -> 3) smoke tests -> 4) flip traffic for canary -> monitor 15m -> promote if green, else rollback.

deploy-bot: scheduled publish job queued by alex for 1815001140. targets: @cohort-A, channels: npm:@canary, pip:staging. :robot_face:

mica: noted. i'll be on watch for telemetry and cost spikes.

jen: holding on - registry returned 409 on an earlier npm publish attempt, seen locally. will try a dry-run now.

samir: flagging a checksum mismatch I just saw on the wheel build for 0.12.3-rc. build server shows different sha256 than artifact store. investigating.

sujay: if checksum mismatch persists -> stop publish and yank the canary. criteria: any binary checksum mismatch OR failing smoke tests >=2/5. also auto-rollback if error rate > 1% on canary.

jen: dry-run succeeded now, no 409. could have been transient registry lock.

qa-bot: smoke tests queued: basic import, init, tokenization, simple generate. expected runtime ~4m. will post results.

alex: reminder: deprecation note for legacy sync client must be in release notes before promote. @mica can you confirm copy landed in docs?

mica: yes, PR #5423 has the deprecation blurb and migration quickstart. docs preview published.

samir: build infra root cause: pypi mirror out-of-sync with internal cache. i re-uploaded corrected wheel, new checksum 0f3a9b... please validate.

jen: npm publish now started (deploy-bot).

deploy-bot: npm publish completed: package @redwood/client-js@0.12.3-canary published -> tag:@canary.

qa-bot: smoke tests: import ok, init ok, tokenization ok, generate: 1/10 timeouts (flaky env). overall PASS (minor flake).

alex: launching pip push to staging now.

deploy-bot: pip wheel upload completed to staging repo (0.12.3rc).

samir: rechecked wheel checksum matches my corrected build. good.

mica: telemetry baseline looks normal. latency within SLO on canary. no error bump.

jen: quick note - npm tag pinned successfully. publishing release notes draft to /release-notes/0.12.3-canary.md

alex: monitoring 15m window. if we keep green, schedule promote at +20m.

sujay: reminder for rollback steps (copied here):
```
# rollback quick steps
npm dist-tag add @redwood/client-js@previous stable
npm deprecate @redwood/client-js@0.12.3-canary "canary rolled back due to issues"
pip index remove 0.12.3rc --repo staging (manual)
revert canary routing in infra: /infra/feature-flags -> unset client_js_canary
```

jen: also keep the release branch available for hotfix republish if needed.

deploy-bot: health check probe on canary beat every 30s. next probe in 30s.

qa-bot: second smoke run scheduled because of timeout earlier.

qa-bot: second smoke: all tests PASS.

mica: rolling metrics look stable. no anomalies.

alex: thumbs. proceeding to promote to 25% at +20m, then gradual. will update release notes with GA timing.

samir: can we add an emergency kill script to ops-runbook? small one-liner to yank tag and revert routing.

alex: yes, adding to runbook now. one-liner for ops: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/feature-flags/client_js_canary -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'`

jen: document updated with deprec note and canary timeline.

deploy-bot: canary promoted: routing set to 25% for cohort-A.

mica: alerting configured for 0.5% error spike, will page on-call.

sujay: all good from my side. if anything fails, follow rollback steps above.

alex: thanks everyone. final GA plan: wait 2h, run final perf/regression suite, then full promote if green. posting follow-up thread for GA. :shipit:
